section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the header and date for the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Toldos,
Rosh Chodesh and Erev Rosh Chodesh Kislev,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section notes the difficulty that the blessing "And may G-d give you" uses the name Elokim, while blessings typically use the name Havayah.
section.t: "And may G-d give you from the dew of the heavens and from the fat of the land, etc."¹
And the precise point in this is known,²
for all blessings are from the Name Havayah,
for the Name Elokim is the attribute of judgment and contraction, and blessings, whose essence is drawing down and influence, are from the Name Havayah,
and like the Priestly Blessing, in each of its three verses³
the Name Havayah is mentioned,
yet in this blessing it says "And may G-d give you" [using Elokim].
And one may add,
that this precise point
(that regarding a blessing the Name Elokim is mentioned)
is also in the first blessing with which Yitzchak was blessed after the death of Avraham, as it is written⁴
"And G-d blessed Yitzchak his son."
For in all the blessings with which the Holy One, blessed be He, blessed Avraham⁵
[and also in the blessings with which He blessed Yitzchak afterwards⁶]
the Name Havayah is stated,
and from this it is implied
that the first blessing with which He blessed Yitzchak, in which it says "And G-d blessed," and the blessing with which Yitzchak blessed [Yaakov], "And may G-d give you," are related to each other.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the influence drawn from gevurah is greater than that from chassadim, and therefore Yitzchak, who is gevurah, gave such elevated blessings.
section.t: And one may say the point of the explanation of this according to what is explained in the Siddur
(with the Torah of Chassidus)
Shaar HaTekios,⁷
that the influence drawn from the gevurot is greater than the influence drawn from the chassadim.
For chassadim are by nature cold, and therefore the influence from them is with limitation,
in contrast to the gevurot, which are with heat,
the influence from them is in a manner of intensification,
to the point of limitless abundance.
And based on this, it explains there that specifically Yitzchak blessed with such elevated blessings
(from the dew of the heavens and from the fat of the land, etc.),
which we do not find such blessings with Avraham nor with Yaakov,
for Yitzchak is gevurah,⁸
and therefore the blessings of Yitzchak are with great abundance.
And based on this, one may explain the verse⁴
"And it was after the death of Avraham, and G-d blessed Yitzchak his son,"
that during Avraham's lifetime
(the aspect of chesed⁸)
the aspect of chesed from above shone,
and after the death of Avraham,
when the conduct
(including the conduct above)
was according to the attribute of Yitzchak,
gevurah,
the blessings were drawn from the gevurot of the Name Elokim,⁹
which are more elevated blessings than the blessings drawn from the chassadim.
And this is also that in Yitzchak's blessing to Yaakov it is written "And may G-d give you" [using Elokim],
that the influence will be with abundance and intensification.
